tests.title: In a git work tree the file view lists tracked and untracked-not-ignored files unquoted, drops ignored and deleted files, and is sorted
given: a temporary git repo built like gitx newRepo (skipped when git is missing)

a tracked file `a b.txt`, an untracked file `é/ü.go`, a file matched by .gitignore, a tracked file deleted from the working tree, a `.agent-fox/x` file and a tracked path under `.git`-like name `sub/.gitkeep`
tests.when: the checks package builds the file view for the repo dir
then: the view contains `a b.txt` and `é/ü.go` byte-exact, unquoted
the ignored file and the deleted tracked file are absent
nothing under `.git/` or `.agent-fox/` is present
paths are slash-separated, relative and sorted in byte order
tests.pseudocode: v = FileView(ctx, dir); assert 'a b.txt' in v; assert 'é/ü.go' in v; assert 'ignored.log' not in v; assert 'deleted.txt' not in v; assert v == sorted(v); assert none(p.startswith('.agent-fox/') or p.startswith('.git/') for p in v)

tests.title: Outside a git work tree the file view is a standard-library walk that skips the fixed directory names
given: a plain temporary directory (no .git) holding src/a.go and, inside it, directories .git, .hg, .svn, node_modules, vendor, target, dist, build, __pycache__, .venv, venv and .agent-fox each with a file
a nested `src/vendor/x.go`
tests.when: the checks package builds the file view for the directory
then: the view is exactly the files outside the skipped directory names (including `src/` content that is not skipped)
no path has any skipped name as a directory segment, at any depth
paths are slash-separated, relative and sorted
tests.pseudocode: v = FileView(ctx, dir); assert v == ['src/a.go']; for p in v: assert not (set(p.split('/')[:-1]) & SKIP)

tests.title: Every file view is sorted, slash-separated, relative and free of .git/ and .agent-fox/ entries
given: a generator of directory trees with random names including spaces and non-ASCII, both inside and outside a git work tree
tests.when: for any generated tree, the file view is built
then: paths are in ascending byte order with no duplicates
no path begins with `/`, contains a backslash, or starts with `.git/` or `.agent-fox/`
tests.pseudocode: for tree in gen_trees(): v = FileView(tree); assert v == sorted(set(v)); assert all(not p.startswith(('/', '.git/', '.agent-fox/')) and '\\' not in p for p in v)

tests.title: The tree hash is 64 lowercase hex characters and reflects file kind, executable bit, symlink target and special file types
given: a temporary directory with a regular file, a symlink to a missing target, and (where the OS allows) a named pipe
tests.when: the tree hash is computed, then the exec bit of the file is flipped, then the symlink target is changed, then recomputed
then: each hash matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$
flipping the executable bit changes the hash
changing the symlink target changes the hash and the dangling link does not fail the call
the named pipe contributes only its type and the call does not block
tests.pseudocode: h1 = TreeHash(dir); assert re.match('^[0-9a-f]{64}$', h1); chmod +x f; assert TreeHash(dir) != h1; relink(l, 'other'); assert TreeHash(dir) != h2

tests.title: The tree hash depends only on the file view's content, never on HEAD, location or ignored files, and any one-byte change alters it
given: a generator of small file sets with random content, exec bits and symlinks
two git repos with different commit histories and absolute locations
tests.when: for any file set written into two repos with different HEADs and locations, with arbitrary content added to ignored files in one, and then one byte of one viewed file is changed
then: the two hashes are equal
the hash after changing one byte of a viewed file differs from before
the hash after changing only ignored files equals the one before
tests.pseudocode: for fs in gen_filesets(): a=mk(fs, history=1); b=mk(fs, history=3); write_ignored(b); assert TreeHash(a)==TreeHash(b); flip_byte(a, pick(fs)); assert TreeHash(a)!=TreeHash(b)

tests.title: An unreadable file hashes as a fixed unreadable marker and does not fail the tree hash
given: a directory with a readable file and a file with mode 000 (test skipped when running as root)
tests.when: the tree hash is computed twice
then: the call returns a hash and a nil error both times
the hash is identical on both calls
making the file readable changes the hash
tests.pseudocode: h, err = TreeHash(dir); assert err == nil; assert h == TreeHash(dir)[0]; chmod 644; assert TreeHash(dir)[0] != h

tests.title: Computing a tree hash creates .agent-fox/ with its .gitignore so the directory never shows in git status
given: a git repo with no .agent-fox directory
tests.when: a tree hash is computed and then a gate result is written under .agent-fox/gate
then: `.agent-fox/.gitignore` exists with the spec-05 content
`git status --porcelain` lists nothing under `.agent-fox/`
a second call with the directory present leaves the .gitignore unchanged
tests.pseudocode: TreeHash(dir); assert exists('.agent-fox/.gitignore'); mkdir('.agent-fox/gate/x'); assert '.agent-fox' not in git('status','--porcelain')

tests.title: gitx ChangedPaths returns diff-from-ref plus untracked paths NUL-separated, byte-exact, de-duplicated and sorted
given: a git repo with a base commit
after it: a modified tracked file ` lead.txt` with a leading space, a new committed file `é x.go`, an untracked `trail .txt ` and an ignored file
tests.when: ChangedPaths(ctx, base) is called
then: the result holds the three paths byte-exact with spaces and non-ASCII preserved
the ignored file is absent
there are no duplicates and the list is sorted
tests.pseudocode: p = g.ChangedPaths(ctx, base); assert p == sorted([' lead.txt','é x.go','trail .txt '])

tests.title: lang detect counts languages from the file view ordered by count then name and reports an empty directory as empty
given: a repo with 3 .go files, 2 .py files, 2 .rs files and 1 .md file, plus go.mod
an empty directory
tests.when: project detection runs on each directory
then: languages are go(3), python(2), rust(2) in that order (ties by name) and markdown is not listed
go carries manifest `go.mod`
for the empty directory `languages` is empty and `gate.checks` is empty, status done
tests.pseudocode: r = Detect(dir); assert [l.name for l in r.languages]==['go','python','rust']; assert r.languages[0].manifest=='go.mod'; assert Detect(empty).gate.checks==[]

tests.title: A parsing gate.json is the effective table with source file
given: a repo with a Makefile `check` target and `.agent-fox/gate.json` = {"version":1,"checks":[one custom check `./ci.sh`]}
tests.when: detection runs
then: `gate.source` is `file`
`gate.checks` is exactly the custom check, not `make check`
tests.pseudocode: r = Detect(dir); assert r.gate.source=='file'; assert [c.argv for c in r.gate.checks]==[['./ci.sh']]

tests.title: Without gate.json the table is detected from root files with Makefile precedence, and this repository gives exactly make check
given: fixtures: a Makefile with `check:`; a GNUmakefile with `test:` and `lint:`; a makefile with only `test:`; a go.mod with a Makefile that has `VAR := x` and `.PHONY` lines only; this repository's root
tests.when: detection runs on each fixture
then: `check` target gives exactly [make check] with kind `check` and source `Makefile:check`
test+lint gives [make lint (lint), make test (test)]; test only gives [make test]
assignments and .PHONY are not targets, so the go.mod fixture falls through to `go vet ./...` then `go test ./...`
`gate.source` is `detected` and every check has name, argv without shell, kind, source and available
on this repository languages[0] is `go` and the checks are exactly [make check]
tests.pseudocode: assert Detect(repoRoot).gate.checks == [Check('make check', ['make','check'], 'check', 'Makefile:check')]

tests.title: Go, Rust, Java and Node manifests yield exactly their listed checks
given: fixtures: go.mod; Cargo.toml; pom.xml without and with mvnw; build.gradle without and with gradlew; package.json with pnpm-lock.yaml and scripts test+lint; yarn.lock and bun.lockb variants; package.json with npm's placeholder test script `echo \"Error: no test specified\" && exit 1`; package.json with no lockfile
tests.when: detection runs on each fixture (no Makefile)
then: Go: go vet ./... (lint), go test ./... (test)
Rust: cargo test
Maven: `mvn -q test`, or `./mvnw test` when mvnw exists; Gradle: `gradle test` or `./gradlew test`
pnpm: `pnpm test` and `pnpm run lint`; yarn and bun use their program; no lockfile uses npm
the npm placeholder test script yields no test check
a package with no lint script yields no lint check
tests.pseudocode: assert argvs(Detect(pnpmFixture)) == [['pnpm','test'],['pnpm','run','lint']]; assert argvs(Detect(placeholder)) == []

tests.title: Python manifests choose pytest or unittest, the uv or poetry prefix, and ruff when configured
given: fixtures: pyproject.toml with uv.lock and `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` and `[tool.ruff]`; pyproject.toml with poetry.lock and pytest in requirements; setup.py only; tox.ini with a root conftest.py; pytest.ini only
tests.when: detection runs on each fixture
then: uv fixture: `uv run pytest` and `uv run ruff check .` (lint)
poetry fixture: `poetry run pytest`
setup.py only: `python -m unittest discover`
conftest.py, pytest.ini or requirements mention each select pytest
tests.pseudocode: assert argvs(Detect(uvFx)) == [['uv','run','pytest'],['uv','run','ruff','check','.']]; assert argvs(Detect(setupOnly)) == [['python','-m','unittest','discover']]

tests.title: suite and programs are de-duplicated in first-seen order and on this repository contain the make and go forms
given: this repository's root
a fixture with a Makefile `check` target plus go.mod and Cargo.toml
tests.when: detection runs
then: on this repo `suite` contains `make check`, `make test`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...`; `programs` contains `make` and `go`
in the fixture `suite` holds the gate argv, then make check/test forms, then language full-suite forms, each once
`programs` starts with the checks' argv[0] and then adds toolchain programs such as `cargo`, without duplicates
tests.pseudocode: r = Detect(repo); assert ['make','check'] in r.suite and ['go','test','./...'] in r.suite; assert 'make' in r.programs and 'go' in r.programs; assert len(set(map(tuple,r.suite)))==len(r.suite)

tests.title: A gate.json that does not parse or names another version fails with category config naming the file
given: the af binary's lang detect command on a repo with a Makefile
case A: .agent-fox/gate.json holds `{not json`; case B: {"version":2,"checks":[]}
tests.when: `af lang detect --dir repo` runs in each case
then: status is `failed` and the exit code is 1
error.category is `config`
error.message contains the path of gate.json
no detected table is returned (no fallback to the Makefile)
tests.pseudocode: env, code = af('lang','detect','--dir',d); assert code==1 and env.status=='failed' and env.error.category=='config' and 'gate.json' in env.error.message

tests.title: The selected checks, their order and argv are identical whatever is on PATH
given: a fixture with go.mod and package.json (pnpm) and Cargo.toml
a generator of PATH values (empty, real, random subsets of the toolchain programs)
tests.when: for any PATH value, detection runs
then: names, argv, kinds and order of checks are equal across all PATH values
only the `available` flags differ
tests.pseudocode: base = strip_available(Detect(fx, PATH=real)); for p in gen_paths(): assert strip_available(Detect(fx, PATH=p)) == base

tests.title: A selected check whose program is missing stays in the table as unavailable with a check_unavailable warning
given: a repo with a Cargo.toml and PATH lacking `cargo`
tests.when: `af lang detect --dir repo` runs
then: status `done`, exit 0
`cargo test` is present with `available: false`
a warning with code `check_unavailable` names the check
tests.pseudocode: env = af('lang','detect'); assert env.status=='done'; assert any(w.code=='check_unavailable' for w in env.warnings)

tests.title: --write stores the freshly detected table atomically, ignoring any existing gate.json, and a later detect reads it back as file
given: a repo with a Makefile `check` target and an existing gate.json naming a different check
tests.when: `af lang detect --write` runs, then `af lang detect` runs again
then: gate.json holds {"version":1,"checks":[make check]} with no leftover temporary files in `.agent-fox/`
the second run reports `gate.source` `file` and the same checks
tests.pseudocode: af('lang','detect','--write'); j=load('.agent-fox/gate.json'); assert j.version==1 and j.checks[0].argv==['make','check']; assert af('lang','detect').result.gate.source=='file'

tests.title: A gate run executes available checks in order, writes one full log each, and records statuses, exit codes, durations and tails
given: a git repo with gate.json holding checks: `pass` (exit 0, prints 100 lines), `fail` (exit 3), `missing` (program that does not exist but is listed available:false... plus a check whose argv[0] exists in PATH only via a script that is removed before start to give error), and `slow` (sleeps past its per-check deadline in an internal test with a short deadline)
tests.when: checks.Run executes the table under ReducedEnvRunner
then: logs exist at `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/01-<slug>.log`, `02-…` for each executed check and hold the full output
pass has status `pass`, exit_code 0; fail has status `fail`, exit_code 3; a program that cannot start has status `error`, exit_code -1; the slow check has status `timeout`
`log` is relative to the dir; `tail` has at most 40 lines and at most 4096 bytes
an unavailable check appears in `skipped` with reason `unavailable` and has no log
tests.pseudocode: r = Run(ctx, dir, opts); assert r.checks[0].status=='pass'; assert len(r.checks[0].tail.splitlines())<=40 and len(r.checks[0].tail)<=4096; assert read(dir+'/'+r.checks[0].log).count('\n')==100

tests.title: --hermetic runs under HermeticRunner with a temporary HOME that is removed afterwards, including after cancellation
given: a check script that writes `$HOME` to a file under the repo's .agent-fox/gate log
a second check that blocks until cancelled
tests.when: a gate run with Hermetic=true completes, and another is cancelled mid-run
then: result has `hermetic: true`
the HOME the script saw is not the real HOME and does not exist after the command returns
after the cancelled run its HOME also does not exist
tests.pseudocode: r = Run(hermetic=true); h = read_log(r).home; assert r.hermetic and h != os.Getenv('HOME') and not exists(h)

tests.title: The result carries all fields and passed is true only when at least one check ran and all executed checks passed
given: tables: all pass; one fail; one pass plus one unavailable skipped; no available check
tests.when: a gate run produces each result
then: every result has id, tree, table_source, hermetic, label, cached, passed, checks and skipped with a reason per entry
passed is true for all-pass and for pass+skipped, false for one fail, false for no executed check
tests.pseudocode: assert Run(allPass).passed; assert not Run(oneFail).passed; assert not Run(noneAvailable).passed

tests.title: A red gate and an empty table are both done with exit 0 and passed false, the empty table with a no_checks warning
given: case A: gate.json with one check `exit 1`; case B: gate.json whose only check program is not on PATH
tests.when: `af gate run --dir repo` runs in each case
then: A: status `done`, exit 0, result.passed false, one check with status fail, no warning no_checks
B: status `done`, exit 0, result.passed false, `checks` empty, skipped lists the check, warning code `no_checks`, no check was executed
tests.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','run'); assert code==0 and env.status=='done' and env.result.passed==false; assert 'no_checks' in codes(env.warnings) for case B

tests.title: A tree changed by the checks is stored under the earlier hash with a tree_changed_during_gate warning
given: a git repo whose single check appends a line to a tracked file
tests.when: `af gate run` runs
then: status `done`
warning code `tree_changed_during_gate`
result.tree equals the tree hash taken before the run and the result is stored under that id
the tree hash now differs from result.tree
tests.pseudocode: pre = TreeHash(dir); env = af('gate','run'); assert env.result.tree == pre; assert TreeHash(dir) != pre; assert exists('.agent-fox/gate/'+env.result.id+'/result.json')

tests.title: A command timeout or signal stops the check's process group, stores no result.json and fails the command
given: gate.json with a check that spawns a child `sleep 60` and waits
`--timeout 1s`, and a second case that sends SIGINT
tests.when: `af gate run --timeout 1s` runs and, separately, the process is signalled
then: status `failed`, exit 1
the sleeping child process no longer exists
`.agent-fox/gate/<id>/result.json` does not exist
a following run with a passing table executes normally (nothing cached from the cancelled run)
tests.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','run','--timeout','1s'); assert code==1 and env.status=='failed'; assert not exists(resultJson); assert not pid_alive(child)

tests.title: The gate id is the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 over tree hash, canonical table JSON and runner mode
given: a fixed tree hash and table
tests.when: the cache key is computed for reduced and hermetic mode, for a reordered-key JSON table, and for a changed table
then: id is 12 lowercase hex characters and equals the first 12 characters of the independently computed SHA-256
reduced and hermetic ids differ
a different table gives a different id
the same table with its JSON keys written in another order gives the same id
the result directory is `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/`
tests.pseudocode: k = sha256(tree + canon(table) + 'reduced'); assert Key(tree, table, Reduced).ID == k[:12]; assert Key(..., Hermetic).ID != k[:12]

tests.title: Two gate runs on an unchanged tree execute a counter-script check once and the second is cached
given: a git repo with gate.json whose check is a script that appends a line to an ignored counter file outside the view
tests.when: `af gate run` runs twice
then: the counter file has exactly one line
the first envelope has `cached: false`, the second `cached: true`
both carry the same id and the second reports the stored checks
no new log is written on the second run
tests.pseudocode: a = af('gate','run'); b = af('gate','run'); assert lines(counter)==1; assert not a.result.cached and b.result.cached; assert a.result.id==b.result.id

tests.title: Any one-byte change to a viewed file forces a re-run and any change confined to ignored files is a cache hit
given: a generator of small repos and of mutations; a counter-script check
tests.when: for any tree, a gate run is followed by one mutation (a one-byte change to a random viewed file, or arbitrary edits to ignored files) and another gate run
then: after a viewed-file mutation the counter increments and `cached` is false
after an ignored-file-only mutation the counter does not change and `cached` is true
tests.pseudocode: for t in gen_repos(): Run(t); m = gen_mutation(t); apply(m); r = Run(t); assert r.cached == (m.kind=='ignored')

tests.title: --no-cache re-executes the checks and replaces the stored result
given: a cached result for the tree from a counter-script check
tests.when: `af gate run --no-cache` runs
then: the counter increments
`cached` is false
result.json holds the new run's duration_ms and logs and the id is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: af('gate','run'); af('gate','run','--no-cache'); assert lines(counter)==2; assert load(resultJson).cached==false

tests.title: result.json is written after the logs, atomically, so concurrent runs never leave a partial file
given: a repo with a check taking ~200ms
10 concurrent gate runs with --no-cache on the same tree while a reader repeatedly parses result.json
tests.when: the runs and the reader execute together
then: every successful read of result.json is complete valid JSON
at the end result.json exists and its logs exist
no temporary files remain in `.agent-fox/gate/<id>/`
a result.json never appears before the first log of its run exists
tests.pseudocode: parallel(10, Run(noCache)); while running: if exists(rj): json.load(rj); assert no tmp files

tests.title: --label records the id in labels.json on a miss and on a hit, and the latest result for a label wins
given: a repo with a counter check, no labels.json
tests.when: `af gate run --label baseline` runs, a viewed file is changed, `--label baseline` runs again, then the same tree is run with `--label after` (a hit)
then: result.label equals the label given in each envelope
labels.json maps baseline to the second run's id, not the first
labels.json maps `after` to the same id although the run was a cache hit
labels.json has no temporary file left beside it
tests.pseudocode: r1=af(...,'--label','baseline'); touch(f); r2=af(...,'--label','baseline'); r3=af(...,'--label','after'); L=load(labels); assert L.baseline==r2.id and L.after==r3.id and r3.cached

tests.title: An invalid or id-shaped label is a usage error before any check runs and leaves labels.json unchanged
given: a repo with an existing labels.json and a counter check
tests.when: `af gate run --label X` runs for labels `Bad`, `1abc`, `a` repeated 33 times, empty-with-space `a b`, and `0123456789ab` (12 hex)
then: status `usage`, exit 2 in every case
the counter file is unchanged (no check ran)
labels.json bytes are unchanged
a valid label `ok_label-1` is accepted
tests.pseudocode: for l in bad: env,code=af('gate','run','--label',l); assert code==2 and env.status=='usage'; assert counter_unchanged and labels_bytes_unchanged

tests.title: Per-check verdicts follow the four-row table with fail, error and timeout all counting as not pass
given: stored results with checks a,b,c,d,e,f whose before/after statuses are pass/pass, fail/pass, pass/fail, fail/fail, error/pass, pass/timeout
one result stored under a label and the other by its id
tests.when: checks.Compare resolves `--before` (label) and `--after` (id) and compares
then: rows are a=pass, b=pass_was_already_failing, c=regressed, d=still_failing, e=pass_was_already_failing, f=regressed
each row carries the before status, after status and verdict
a label that equals a stored id string is resolved as a label first
tests.pseudocode: rows = Compare(dir,'baseline',after.id).rows; assert [r.verdict for r in rows] == [...]

tests.title: The overall verdict is the highest-priority row verdict and landable is true only for pass and pass_was_already_failing
given: a generator of result pairs with the same non-empty check names and random statuses from pass, fail, error, timeout
tests.when: for any such pair, the pair is compared
then: verdict equals the first of regressed, still_failing, pass_was_already_failing, pass that any row carries
landable is true iff verdict is pass or pass_was_already_failing
tests.pseudocode: for (b,a) in gen_pairs(): v = Compare(b,a); assert v.verdict == first(p for p in ORDER if p in rowverdicts(v)); assert v.landable == (v.verdict in ('pass','pass_was_already_failing'))

tests.title: A result with no checks on either side compares as unverified and not landable
given: stored results: one with checks and one with an empty checks list, in both orders; and both empty
tests.when: Compare runs for each combination
then: verdict is `unverified` and landable false in each
no error is returned
tests.pseudocode: assert Compare(empty, full).verdict=='unverified' and not .landable

tests.title: gate compare returns a done envelope with exit 0 and both sides' id, label and passed for each of the five verdicts
given: a repo where gate runs, labelled, have produced result pairs for pass, pass_was_already_failing, regressed, still_failing, and (with an empty-table gate.json) unverified
tests.when: `af gate compare --before B --after A` runs for each pair
then: status `done` and exit 0 in each of the five cases
result holds before{id,label,passed}, after{id,label,passed}, verdict, landable and the rows
verdict equals the expected one in each case and landable is true only for pass and pass_was_already_failing
tests.pseudocode: for pair in pairs: env,code = af('gate','compare','--before',pair.b,'--after',pair.a); assert code==0 and env.status=='done' and env.result.verdict==pair.expected

tests.title: A missing or unresolved --before/--after is a usage error naming the argument
given: a repo with one stored label `baseline`
tests.when: `af gate compare` runs with no --before; with `--before baseline` and no --after; with `--before baseline --after nosuch`
then: status `usage`, exit 2 each time
error.message names `--before` for the first, `--after` for the second, and `nosuch` for the third
tests.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','compare','--before','baseline','--after','nosuch'); assert code==2 and 'nosuch' in env.error.message

tests.title: Results with different check names cannot be compared and the message lists the one-sided names
given: two stored results from different tables: {lint,test} and {test,build}
tests.when: `af gate compare` runs on them
then: status `usage`, exit 2
error.message lists `lint` as only before and `build` as only after
tests.pseudocode: env,code = af('gate','compare',...); assert code==2 and 'lint' in msg and 'build' in msg

tests.title: revert-check refuses a non-top-level --dir, a missing --since and an unresolvable --since before touching any file
given: a git repo with a subdirectory and an untouched tree, index and .agent-fox
tests.when: `af revert-check --since HEAD --dir repo/sub`, `af revert-check` with no --since, and `--since nosuchref` run
then: status `usage`, exit 2 in each
error.message names `--dir`, `--since` and `--since` respectively
tree hash and index bytes are unchanged and no `.agent-fox/revert/` directory was created
tests.pseudocode: for args in cases: env,code = af(*args); assert code==2 and env.status=='usage'; assert state_unchanged()

tests.title: Test-path classification follows the fixed convention table
given: a table of positive and negative paths
tests.when: project.IsTestPath is applied to each
then: true for `a_test.go`, `pkg/testdata/x.json`, `test_a.py`, `a_test.py`, `conftest.py`, `a.test.ts`, `b.spec.js`, `__tests__/x.js`, `src/test/java/A.java`, `FooTest.java`, `FooTests.java`, `FooIT.java`, `x_spec.rb`, `x_test.rb`, `tests/a.rs`, `spec/x.rb`, `a/test/b.c`
false for `main.go`, `latest.go`, `contest.py`, `src/main/java/A.java`, `testing.md` and `attest/x.go`
tests.pseudocode: for p in pos: assert IsTestPath(p); for p in neg: assert not IsTestPath(p)

tests.title: Nothing-to-measure cases return their outcome without modifying any file
given: a git repo with a base commit and gate.json with a test check
case A: no changes; B: only test files changed; C: only non-test files changed; D: test and non-test changed but gate.json has only a lint check
tests.when: `af revert-check --since base` runs in each case
then: status `done`, exit 0, restored true
outcomes are no_changes, no_code_changes, no_test_changes and inconclusive respectively
warning `fix_not_proven` is present for B, C and D and absent for A
tree hash and index bytes are unchanged and no gate check ran in the reverted state
tests.pseudocode: for c in cases: env = af('revert-check','--since',base); assert env.result.outcome==c.outcome; assert ('fix_not_proven' in codes) == (c.outcome!='no_changes'); assert unchanged()

tests.title: A red current tree is inconclusive with reason after_not_green and nothing is reverted
given: a git repo whose change touches a source file and a test file, and whose test check fails on the current tree
tests.when: `af revert-check --since base` runs
then: status `done`, outcome `inconclusive`, reason `after_not_green`, closes false

tests.title: Non-test paths are reverted to the ref's content and mode without touching the index, added files are moved aside and test paths stay
given: a base commit with `lib.sh` (mode 755, content v1) and a test script `check_test.sh`

a gate.json test check that, when run, records whether lib.sh holds v1, whether new.go exists and whether fix_test.go exists, into an ignored file
tests.when: `af revert-check --since base` runs
then: during the reverted run lib.sh held v1 with mode 755, new.go did not exist and fix_test.go existed

the backup under `.agent-fox/revert/<id>/` held a manifest and copies while reverted
`git diff --cached` was empty and the index was untouched throughout
only test/check kind checks ran on the reverted tree
tests.pseudocode: env = af('revert-check','--since',base); obs = read(observation); assert obs.libContent=='v1' and obs.libMode==0o755 and not obs.newExists and obs.testExists; assert env.result.reverted_files==['lib.sh','new.go']

tests.title: proven and not_proven both exit 0 with closes true only for proven and the full result shape
given: fixture P: change adds a fix to lib file and a test that fails without it

tests.pseudocode: p = af(P); assert p.result.outcome=='proven' and p.result.closes and len(p.result.since)==40; n = af(N); assert n.result.outcome=='not_proven' and not n.result.closes

tests.title: Every outcome leaves the tree hash and the index bytes as they were

tests.title: A signal or timeout during the reverted run still restores the tree and the index
